ground_truth_core_content:
Introduction:
**1:** Both sections cover the same evolution story (2022 chatbots, 2023 RAG, 2024 tool-using agents, 2025-now memory-enabled agents), the same last-lesson callback, the same prompt-engineering-limits framing, and the same context-engineering-as-orchestration definition. Citations are added throughout but layer on top of the same ideas rather than replacing any of them.

From Prompt to Context Engineering:
**1:** Both sections cover the same five beats in the same substance: single-interaction design, context decay, the physical window limit plus cost/latency, the recent-project anecdote, and the transition to context engineering. No expected idea is absent.

Understanding Context Engineering:
**1:** Both sections cover the definition/optimization-problem framing with the cooking-agent example, the Karpathy CPU/RAM analogy, the prompt-engineering-subset relationship, the comparison table, the fine-tuning argument, the decision-making diagram, the Slack example, and the closing course reference. The generated section adds a training-time-vs-inference-time distinction and an explicit textual enumeration of the decision order, both layered additions rather than substitutions.

What Makes Up the Context:
**1:** Both sections cover the workflow description, the two memory categories, and — despite being written as flowing prose with bold lead-ins rather than bulleted lists — all four Short-Term Working Memory elements (user input, message history, internal thoughts, action-call outputs) and all three Long-Term Memory types (procedural, episodic, semantic) with matching descriptions, plus the 'bear with us' aside and the closing dynamic-recomputation point. CoreContent is about substance, not formatting, so the bullets-to-prose conversion does not affect this score (see Structure).

Production Implementation Challenges:
**1:** Both sections cover the same restated core question and the same four challenges in the same substance: the window/RAM analogy (with an added quadratic-attention-cost point), lost-in-the-middle information overload (with an added 30%+ degradation statistic), context drift as conflicting facts (with a different toy example — budget figures instead of cat colors — illustrating the same generic concept), and the two-part tool-confusion explanation. No expected idea is absent.

Key Strategies for Context Optimization:
**1:** Both sections cover all four strategies with matching substance: Selecting the Right Context (structured outputs, RAG, reducing actions, temporal ranking, repeating instructions — all five present, just prose-merged rather than bulleted), Context Compression (summaries, moving preferences to episodic memory, deduplication, plus an added token-reduction statistic), Isolating Context (splitting across agents, orchestrator-worker), and Format Optimizations (XML tags, YAML). No expected idea is absent despite the formatting change (see Structure).

Practical Example:
**0:** The query walkthrough and code-example lead-in are present, and the tech-stack list covers all four required elements. However, two of the four expected use cases lose their specific substance entirely: the guideline/ground-truth idea that Project Task Managers 'automatically understand project requirements, add and update project tasks' and that a Content Creator Assistant uses 'your research, past content, and personality traits' are never stated anywhere in the generated section — only the Financial Services case gets an actual description, while Healthcare, Project Management, and Content Creator are reduced to bare name-drops in the opening sentence. Separately and consistent with the standing ruling on this section, the expected section's concrete, YAML-formatted, multi-step code walkthrough (real patient/literature data, an explicit demonstration of YAML formatting, and a final rendered prompt) is absent — the generated code block is a single abstract template with placeholder variables and no YAML shown, despite the surrounding prose claiming the example demonstrates 'how we used YAML to format input data collections.' Two independent, substantive gaps (the dropped use-case descriptions and the missing concrete/YAML worked example) drive this score.

Connecting Context Engineering to AI Engineering:
**1:** Both sections cover the cannot-learn-in-isolation framing, the course-goal paragraph, and the transition to the next lesson (expanded here to also forward-reference structured outputs' role and memory/RAG/actions). The four-domain breakdown is present with matching substance for AI Engineering, Software Engineering, and Data Engineering; the fourth domain is labeled 'MLOps' here instead of 'Operations (Ops)' but covers the same deployment/CI-CD/reproducibility substance, so this is treated as a terminology substitution rather than a content mismatch. Per the standing ruling on this section, the dropped opening 'more of an art than a science' framing sentence is not treated as a missing substantive idea since the intuition-based description immediately following it is preserved nearly verbatim.

References:
**1:** Both sections contain a numbered list of references serving the same bibliographic purpose for the article.
